title: Dataproc -- managed Spark clusters, jobs, cost management
exp: Dataproc is GCP's managed Hadoop/Spark service -- the direct equivalent of EMR, sharing much of EMR's cluster-lifecycle vocabulary since both are built on the same open-source Hadoop ecosystem foundations.
pts: Dataproc cluster: Master node(s) + Worker nodes, structurally identical to EMR's Master/Core split -- Dataproc calls the data-holding compute nodes simply 'Workers' rather than distinguishing Core vs Task the way EMR does.

Secondary Workers (Dataproc's Preemptible or Spot VM worker pool) are the direct equivalent of EMR Task nodes on Spot Instances -- safe for compute-only work that can be retried, never for data-critical roles.

Ephemeral clusters: created just before a job runs and deleted immediately after, via a single gcloud dataproc clusters create with a job attached and --delete-cluster-on-completion-style workflow -- the Dataproc equivalent of an EMR transient cluster with auto-terminate.

Dataproc Serverless for Spark removes cluster management entirely -- submit a batch workload, GCP provisions and tears down compute automatically, billed per resource-second -- the direct equivalent of EMR Serverless.

Dataproc Workflow Templates define a multi-step job DAG (create cluster, run job, delete cluster) as a single reusable resource -- somewhat like combining an EMR cluster definition and its Steps into one deployable unit.
Cluster autoscaling policies can be attached to a Dataproc cluster to scale worker count based on YARN pending memory, the same underlying signal EMR's managed scaling uses.
code:
# Ephemeral cluster + job in one workflow -- the Dataproc "transient EMR" pattern
gcloud dataproc clusters create orders-pipeline-cluster \
  --region=us-central1 \
  --master-machine-type=n2-standard-4 \
  --worker-machine-type=n2-standard-4 \
  --num-workers=2 \
  --num-secondary-workers=4 \
  --secondary-worker-type=spot

gcloud dataproc jobs submit pyspark gs://bucket/scripts/validate.py \
  --cluster=orders-pipeline-cluster --region=us-central1

# Delete when done -- the equivalent discipline to terminating an EMR cluster
gcloud dataproc clusters delete orders-pipeline-cluster --region=us-central1 --quiet

# Dataproc Serverless -- no cluster to manage at all
gcloud dataproc batches submit pyspark gs://bucket/scripts/validate.py \
  --region=us-central1 \
  --batch=orders-pipeline-batch

# Workflow Template -- reusable create-run-delete DAG as one resource
gcloud dataproc workflow-templates create orders-pipeline-template --region=us-central1
gcloud dataproc workflow-templates set-managed-cluster orders-pipeline-template \
  --region=us-central1 --cluster-name=ephemeral-cluster \
  --num-workers=2 --worker-machine-type=n2-standard-4
pr: Create an ephemeral Dataproc cluster with Secondary Workers, submit a PySpark job, and delete the cluster -- matching the transient EMR cluster exercise

r: Ephemeral cluster, explicit delete or Workflow Template

qa.q: What is the Dataproc equivalent of an EMR transient cluster with auto-terminate, and what command pattern achieves it?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** An ephemeral cluster -- created immediately before a job with gcloud dataproc clusters create, the job submitted against it, then explicitly deleted with gcloud dataproc clusters delete right after. Dataproc Workflow Templates can also encode this entire create-run-delete sequence as a single reusable resource, which is arguably a cleaner abstraction than manually scripting the equivalent sequence of EMR CLI calls.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Transient creates a new instance on every request; Scoped creates one instance per HTTP request container; Singleton lives for the app domain lifespan. Capturing a Scoped service inside a Singleton captures the DbContext across requests, causing concurrency bugs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Instantiating new HttpClient() instances manually causes socket exhaustion in OS TIME_WAIT state under high concurrency. Fix: register typed clients with IHttpClientFactory to manage handler lifetimes and DNS refresh.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** IHttpClientFactory prevents socket leaks and manages DNS rotation, but requires explicit Polly retry and circuit breaker policies to prevent cascade failures during downstream outages.

qa.q: How do Dataproc's Secondary Workers compare to EMR's Task nodes, and what is the safety rule that carries over unchanged?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Secondary Workers are Dataproc's Spot/Preemptible-backed compute-only worker pool, structurally equivalent to EMR Task nodes on Spot Instances. The exact same safety rule applies: Secondary Workers are safe for retriable compute-only work because a reclaimed VM just causes Spark to reschedule the affected tasks, but they should never host anything data-critical or serve as the cluster's primary/master role, mirroring the never-Spot-the-core-or-master guidance from the EMR days.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Async methods compile into an IAsyncStateMachine struct managed by the AsyncMethodBuilder. Awaiting an uncompleted task yields execution back to the caller. Blocking with .Result on a thread bound to a SynchronizationContext causes deadlocks when the continuation waits for the blocked thread.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Sync-over-async (.Result or .Wait()) on ASP.NET request threads rapidly exhausts thread pool threads, leading to HTTP 503 gateway timeouts and request queuing under load.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Async all the way preserves thread pool scalability, but requires passing CancellationToken through all layers and avoiding sync blocking methods everywhere.
